title: the planted faults (V17 on the in-process box)
note: Written by hand from the drill's record (python -m tools.planted_faults run; tests/e2e/test_planted_faults_drill.py holds the fault-by-surface table). Box: the in-process console, no Docker. fault: the drill's fault key; surface: first page, mail, metrics, runbook or all.

findings.claim: A backup target that cannot be written shows on /metrics (backup red) and in the mail, but on no line of the administrator's first page; the Backups tile stays green.
findings.expected: plan 8 criterion 4 and V17: one red line on the first page, the same in the mail and /metrics

findings.claim: With the NAS share unmounted the nightly backup writes its copy into the empty mount point on the box's own disk and reports ok; every check stays green and no mail goes.
findings.expected: V17 backup target gone; RUNBOOK section 5: the copies go to the NAS share and the USB disk

findings.claim: A disk 94 % full is red on /metrics and in the mail but on no line of the administrator's first page (the page says disks are in the mail and on /metrics only).
A certificate that ends in 12 days is red on /metrics and in the mail but on no line of the administrator's first page.
The zh-TW and ja health mails and the ja digest translate the health level, then give the failing check in English (backup, disk and certificate faults).
findings.expected: the card's three languages; D-379's translated health line

findings.claim: The health mail and the digest name no runbook page for the disk or the certificate; only the backup's own alert mail names RUNBOOK section 5.
findings.expected: V17: each fault has a runbook page that works

findings.claim: A morning whose mails did not go is shown nowhere: no first-page line, no mail, no /metrics check; the product has no check for it.
findings.expected: V17 the morning mail missing; runbook 04 morning mail: users notice first

findings.claim: The runbook's fix, Send notices now, sends N1 and N2 only; a missed 07:00 health mail is not sent again.
A clock 600 s off fails doctor's clock check, but no first-page line, mail or /metrics check shows it, and the runbook has no page for the clock.
With a passing canary of the morning standing, model servers that do not answer change nothing on the first page, in the mail or on /metrics until the canary is 36 h old.
findings.expected: V17 a GPU fault; docs/runbook/04-gpu-fault.md signs

findings.claim: An empty feed folder holds the night correctly but shows on no first-page line, mail or /metrics check, and no runbook page covers an empty or missing feed.
findings.expected: V17's rule applied to the card's seventh fault

findings.claim: The disk-full page's first step runs df on /data, /var/lib/docker and / only; the full disk the health line names by its path is not among them.
findings.expected: docs/runbook/04-disk-full.md:11: note which disk is full

findings.claim: With no passing canary the waiting line shows in all three languages but names no page or step to follow.
findings.expected: V17: each fault has a runbook page that works
